title: Ingrid and the prion specimen (paraphrase)
topic: A laboratory team investigates a prion sample: Ingrid receives a tissue sample with misfolded prions, the microscope shows fibrils that form a plaque, a chaperone protein dissolves an aggregate, a colleague disagrees with the result, and a second test confirms the prion
tail_E: Ingrid is now certain that the sheep suffered from a fatal prion
target_note: Same target as formulation A: 'disease' completes 'the sheep suffered from a fatal prion' after ten units about misfolded prions, fibrils and plaques in sheep tissue ('prion disease' is the standard collocation of the domain). The word and its German equivalents (Krankheit / Erkrankung / Leiden) occur nowhere in the units or the tail, and the competitors 'illness' and 'infection' are absent as well. ' disease' is a single Pythia token (id 2728); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.43, next candidates 'infection' ~ 0.16 and 'illness' ~ 0.06)
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (F19B, prion sample in the laboratory, Ingrid, paraphrase)
notes: Formulation B, domain protein_misfolding: independent re-phrasing of the ten meaning units of F19A in both languages (same events, same order, same name Ingrid). The sample is 'the specimen' / 'das Präparat', the clinic 'the hospital' / 'das Krankenhaus', the colleague 'another researcher' / 'ein anderer Forscher', the result 'the finding' / 'der Befund', the second test 'the repeat test' / 'der Wiederholungstest'; the fibrils clump into plaques (plural) instead of forming one plaque, and the chaperone breaks an aggregate up instead of dissolving it. Domain vocabulary is kept in both languages: Prionen, fehlgefaltet, Fibrillen, Plaques, Chaperonprotein, Aggregat (the compound is closed rather than hyphenated: lsne.lang_id splits words at hyphens, so 'Chaperon-Protein' would contribute a stray English 'Protein'). No separable German verbs ('auseinandernehmen', 'nachweisen', 'hinzufügen' avoided: 'zerlegt', 'belegt', 'gibt ... zum'); 'birgt', 'betrachtet', 'enthüllt', 'verklumpen' and 'hinterfragt' are inseparable. Subjects vary between the protagonist, another researcher and the objects of the experiment (specimen, microscope, fibrils, chaperone, repeat test), singular and plural. Present tense, positive polarity; unit 9 reads naturally in German, units 1 and 10 in English, unit 10 is the closing sentence. The tail keeps the wording of A's probe clause ('the sheep suffered from a fatal prion') on purpose, so that A and B differ in the ten units but are compared on an identical prediction cue; 'Ingrid' is labelled 'N' by lsne.lang_id (not in the lexicon's name list), which costs no accuracy because 'N' labels are excluded.
